title: Marmol has Cards embracing youthful energy, and it's paying off - Show-Me State Times
text:
José Fermín showed his excitement during an in-game interview with Cardinals.TV’s Dani Wexelman on April 29 when Victor Scott II hit a home run in Pittsburgh. Fermín apologized for his loud reaction but continued to cheer for his teammate, highlighting the supportive atmosphere among the St. Louis Cardinals this season.
This camaraderie is notable as the team has shifted toward a younger roster following changes over the winter. Rather than being discouraged by the departure of veteran players, the new core has taken ownership of their roles and encouraged each other to succeed.
Manager Oliver Marmol’s leadership is seen as central to this positive environment. After a comeback win against the Pirates, Marmol was seen celebrating with players and coaches, reflecting strong team spirit. “I think St. Louis likes watching a team that plays the game the right way, that plays the game hard, that never gives in,” Marmol told flagship radio station KMOX. “Those are the things we can control, and we’ll hold ourselves, I’ll hold myself, accountable to. And then let everything else play out. It’s hard not to like this group. It’s hard to watch them and not get excited about their style of play.”
The Cardinals entered Wednesday at 16-13 and third place in their division despite low outside expectations for early success from such an inexperienced group.
Observers note that rebuilding teams typically struggle or lack consistency early on; however, these Cardinals have shown resilience by coming from behind frequently this season.
The approach set by Marmol is shaping what could be a new era for St. Louis baseball as he guides younger players through transition while fostering unity within the clubhouse.
